study_identification.title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

study_characteristics.study_objective: To introduce and validate a whole-brain normative modeling approach for functional connectivity (FC) called Functional Connectivity Integrative Normative Modelling (FUNCOIN), and to demonstrate its utility in identifying brain function abnormalities in bipolar disorder (BD) and Parkinson's disease (PD).

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: UKB ICA parcellation with 55 ICA components

quality_checking_detail.answer: Right-truncated all time series to 490 points followed by removal of the first 8 time points due to large fluctuations.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: The model was retrained with scanner site as an additional (categorical, dummy-coded) covariate to assess site effects. The main analysis focused on components unaffected by site. The authors state that no scanning site effects were found on the Z-scores of the healthy subjects.

predictor_effects.answer: Sex, age, and sex-age interaction were modeled as fixed effects. An alternative model including scanning site as a categorical variable was also explored.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper explicitly addresses nuisance variables like site effects by modeling them and focusing on components unaffected by them.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: In line with earlier normative modelling studies on structural MRI from UKB 37,38 , we found no scanning site effects on the Z -scores of the healthy subjects (see Supplementary text and Supplementary Fig. 6).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model was trained on a large dataset (N=32,000) and validated on a separate test set (N=14,000) from the same domain (UK Biobank). The paper discusses model validation and calibration using the training data.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We use rsfMRI data from UKB ( N >60,000 people) 25 . In this setting, we consider a subject healthy if they have no psychiatric or neurological diagnoses (group F or G diagnoses in ICD-10), which is the case for approximately 50000 of the subjects. We divide the subjects into three groups: A large group of healthy subjects to train the model on (training data, N =32,000), a set of healthy subjects on which we test the out-of-sample performance of the model (test data, N =14,000), and a group of subjects with psychiatric or neurological diagnoses.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The model's out-of-sample performance was tested on an independent set of 14,000 healthy subjects from the UK Biobank.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: With the out-of-sample healthy test subjects, we assess explanatory power and generalizability of the model, while the individual Z -scores of the healthy and diagnosed subjects are used to probe the model's ability to identify subjects with brain disease as outliers.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study did not validate the model on a dataset from a different domain.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Permutation testing with Fisher's exact test to compare the proportion of outliers between diagnosed and healthy groups. Mann-Whitney U test to compare distributions of outlier counts.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: A novel whole-brain normative model (FUNCOIN) identified significant FC abnormalities in individuals with Bipolar Disorder and Parkinson's Disease, even years before a PD diagnosis, outperforming traditional localized models.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The FUNCOIN model revealed that 9.1% of PD patients and 14.8% of BD patients were outliers, with BD patients splitting into two distinct subgroups. Notably, 9.3% of PD patients showed abnormalities up to 7.8 years before diagnosis. In contrast, localized (edgewise) models failed to reliably identify these individuals and suffered from issues of multiple comparisons and lack of specificity.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Challenges in interpreting Z-scores, potential for clinically irrelevant findings, and the fact that some individuals with disease may not be identified as outliers. The study also only considered linear effects on FC.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The FUNCOIN method has potential for subtyping heterogeneous patient groups and for early diagnosis, as demonstrated with pre-diagnosis PD patients.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper introduces a new Python package called 'FUNCOIN' for their modeling approach. The authors also highlight the limitations of traditional edgewise normative models in fMRI.
